user_problem: A scoring rubric has descriptors but lacks concrete synthetic examples showing boundaries between performance levels.
unique_output: A set of short anchor responses with criterion-by-criterion scores and explanations tied to exact rubric language.
required_input: Rubric criteria, level descriptors, prompt, scoring rules, and any non-scorable conditions.
critical_rule: Every score rationale must cite a supplied descriptor; ambiguous boundaries receive paired anchors, not invented standards.
nearest_existing_and_difference: Nearest is example-set-diversifier; this builds scoring anchors rather than diversifying instructional examples.
acceptance_scenario: Input criterion requires a claim plus two relevant facts for level 3 and one fact for level 2. Output provides one synthetic response at each level and identifies the second fact as the observable boundary.
